subject: math
cluster: Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects
skillName: Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects
intro: This cluster worksheet covers visualizing relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects (standard GEO.G-GMD.B.4). The 15 problems ramp from naming cross-sections and solids of revolution in standard position, through reading off dimensions and computing volumes, to multi-step problems with offset axes, conic-section cross-sections, and justifications. Give exact answers in terms of $\pi$ and radicals unless told otherwise.

items.prompt: A right circular cylinder is cut by a plane that is parallel to its circular base. What is the shape of the cross-section?

steps: A plane parallel to the base slices straight across the cylinder.
Every point on the boundary of the slice is the same distance from the central axis as the rim of the base.
Therefore the cross-section is a circle congruent to the base.

items.prompt: A rectangle is rotated $360^\circ$ about one of its sides. Name the three-dimensional solid that is generated.

steps: The side the rectangle spins about is the axis of revolution.
Each point of the rectangle traces a circle around that axis.
Sweeping the rectangle all the way around produces a right circular cylinder.

items.prompt: A plane cuts a sphere. No matter how the plane is tilted, what shape is every cross-section of a sphere?

steps: A sphere is the set of all points a fixed distance from its center.
Any flat plane intersects this set in points all equidistant from the foot of the perpendicular dropped from the center to the plane.
That equidistant set within a plane is a circle, so every cross-section of a sphere is a circle (the largest being a great circle through the center).

items.prompt: A right circular cone is cut by a plane parallel to its circular base (not through the apex). What is the shape of the cross-section?

steps: A plane parallel to the base of a cone slices across the cone at a single height.
At that height the cone has a circular boundary, just smaller than the base.
So the cross-section is a circle (a scaled-down copy of the base).

items.prompt: A right circular cylinder is cut by a plane that passes through its central axis (perpendicular to the base). What is the shape of the cross-section? Do not answer 'circle' without checking the orientation.

steps: A plane through the axis runs vertically down the full height of the cylinder.
It meets the curved surface in two vertical segments and the bases in two horizontal segments.
These four segments meet at right angles, so the cross-section is a rectangle whose width is the diameter and whose height is the cylinder's height.

items.prompt: A cube has edge length $5$. A plane cuts the cube perpendicular to one face and parallel to a set of edges, slicing straight through. Identify the shape of the cross-section and find its area.
items.answer: a square with area $25$ square units

steps: A plane perpendicular to a face and parallel to the edges runs straight from one face to the opposite face.
It is bounded by four edges, each of length $5$, meeting at right angles, so the cross-section is a square.
The side length is $5$, so the area is $5 \times 5 = 25$ square units.

items.prompt: A rectangle with width $4$ and height $6$ is rotated $360^\circ$ about its side of length $6$ (a vertical side). Identify the solid generated and state its radius and height.
items.answer: a cylinder with radius $4$ and height $6$

steps: Rotating a rectangle about one side generates a right circular cylinder.
The height of the cylinder equals the side lying on the axis: $h = 6$.
The radius equals the distance from the axis to the far side, which is the width: $r = 4$.
So the solid is a cylinder with radius $4$ and height $6$.

items.prompt: A right circular cone is cut by a plane that passes through the apex and is perpendicular to the base. What is the shape of the cross-section?

steps: A plane through the apex perpendicular to the base slices the cone vertically through its tip.
It meets the base along a diameter and runs up the two opposite slant sides to the apex.
The two slant sides are equal in length, so the cross-section is an isosceles triangle whose base is the diameter and whose height is the cone's height.

items.prompt: A right triangle has a horizontal leg of length $3$ and a vertical leg of length $8$. The triangle is rotated $360^\circ$ about its vertical leg. Identify the solid and compute its volume exactly.
items.answer: a cone with volume $24\pi$ cubic units

steps: Rotating a right triangle about a leg generates a cone, with that leg as the axis.
The leg on the axis is the height: $h = 8$. The perpendicular leg is the radius: $r = 3$.
Compute: $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi (9)(8) = \frac{1}{3}\pi (72) = 24\pi$ cubic units.

items.prompt: A right circular cylinder is cut by an oblique plane that meets the curved surface at a tilt without touching either base. What is the shape of the cross-section?

steps: A plane parallel to the base would give a circle, but here the plane is tilted.
The tilt stretches the slice along the direction of the tilt while leaving the perpendicular direction the same width.
A circle stretched in one direction is an ellipse, so the cross-section is an ellipse.

items.prompt: A semicircle of radius $5$ is rotated $360^\circ$ about its diameter. Identify the solid generated and find its volume exactly.
items.answer: a sphere with volume $\frac{500}{3}\pi$ cubic units

steps: Rotating a semicircle about its straight diameter sweeps the curved edge all the way around the center.
The result is a sphere whose radius equals the radius of the semicircle: $r = 5$.
Compute: $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi (125) = \frac{500}{3}\pi$ cubic units.

items.prompt: A rectangle with width $2$ and height $10$ is rotated $360^\circ$ about its side of length $10$ (a vertical side). Identify the solid, then compute its volume and total surface area exactly.
items.answer: a cylinder with volume $40\pi$ cubic units and surface area $48\pi$ square units

steps: Rotating the rectangle about its vertical side of length $10$ makes that side the axis, so the height is $h = 10$.
The radius is the distance from the axis to the far side, which is the width: $r = 2$.
Volume: $V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (2)^2 (10) = \pi (4)(10) = 40\pi$ cubic units.
Surface area: $S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h = 2\pi (2)^2 + 2\pi (2)(10) = 8\pi + 40\pi = 48\pi$ square units.

items.prompt: A square of side $3$ is rotated $360^\circ$ about a vertical line that lies $2$ units to the left of the square's nearest (left) side, with the line not passing through the square. Describe the solid generated and find its volume exactly.
items.answer: a hollow cylindrical ring (washer) with inner radius $2$, outer radius $5$, height $3$, and volume $63\pi$ cubic units

steps: Because the axis is offset and does not touch the square, the square sweeps out a hollow ring (a washer).
Inner radius: distance from the axis to the near (left) side, $r = 2$.
Outer radius: distance from the axis to the far (right) side, $R = 2 + 3 = 5$.
Height: the vertical extent of the square, $h = 3$.
Volume is the outer cylinder minus the inner cylinder: $V = \pi (R^2 - r^2) h = \pi (5^2 - 2^2)(3) = \pi (25 - 4)(3) = \pi (21)(3) = 63\pi$ cubic units.

items.prompt: A right circular cone is cut by a plane that is parallel to exactly one slant side of the cone (not through the apex, and not parallel to the base). Classify the conic-section cross-section produced, and briefly justify the answer.

steps: The conic produced by slicing a cone depends on the plane's angle relative to the slant of the cone.
A plane parallel to the base gives a circle; a less steep plane gives an ellipse; a plane steeper than the slant gives a hyperbola.
The boundary case, a plane parallel to exactly one slant side, gives a parabola: the slice does not close up (so it is not an ellipse) yet meets only one nappe of the cone (so it is not a hyperbola).
Therefore the cross-section is a parabola.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs of length $6$ (horizontal) and $8$ (vertical) and hypotenuse $10$. It is rotated $360^\circ$ about its vertical leg. Identify the solid generated, then find its total surface area exactly (lateral surface plus base).
items.answer: a cone with total surface area $96\pi$ square units

steps: Rotating the right triangle about its vertical leg generates a cone with height $h = 8$ and radius $r = 6$ (the horizontal leg).
The slant height of the cone is the hypotenuse of the triangle: $\ell = 10$ (check: $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36+64} = \sqrt{100} = 10$).
Lateral surface area: $\pi r \ell = \pi (6)(10) = 60\pi$.
Base area: $\pi r^2 = \pi (6)^2 = 36\pi$.
Total surface area: $60\pi + 36\pi = 96\pi$ square units.
